strings.do.title: Domains
strings.do.collide.title: variants of the same name: {list} — click to merge
strings.do.tree.intro: A domain is a path, so these are levels: 'acme/x100/p200' files a memory under a routine inside a module inside a product. Asking about a level covers everything below it — so a name in italics is a level nothing was filed on directly, and +n counts what sits underneath.
strings.do.rollupWhy: filed further down this branch, not on this level
strings.do.rn.placeholder: new path (or an existing one, to merge)
strings.do.rn.warn: the target already exists — memories will be merged into it
strings.do.rn.cycle: a domain cannot be moved inside itself
strings.do.rn.pathHint: Write a path to nest it: 'acme/x100' files this domain under 'acme'.
strings.do.rn.subtree: {n} memories in the subdomains move with it, keeping their own levels
strings.do.rn.hint: every affected memory is re-indexed, and the change is kept in the history
strings.do.case.title: Domain casing
strings.do.case.desc: How domain names are stored. Applies to every new write; 'lower'/'upper' adjust the domains that do not match and report it. Use Normalize to bring existing domains in line — it also repairs a path with a blank or padded level.
strings.do.case.preserveHint: Policy is Preserve — nothing to normalize.
strings.do.case.none: All domains already match the policy.
strings.do.norm.title: Normalize domains
strings.do.norm.mergeWarn: Merges combine variant spellings into one domain — the affected memories are re-indexed and the change is kept in the history.

strings.mn.confirm.vacuum: Rewrite the database file to reclaim its free space? The memories are untouched, but the reclaimed pages are gone and this cannot be undone.

strings.op.emptyRuns: no optimization runs yet — from a Claude session say “optimize my memories” and the agent will stage a batch of suggestions here for review
strings.op.allApplied: all suggestions in this run are applied — turn off “hide applied” to see them

strings.op.discardConfirm.title: Discard run
strings.op.discardConfirm.body: Delete run #{id} and all its suggestions? Already-applied changes to memories are NOT reverted — this only clears the suggestion list.
strings.nm.title: New memory
strings.nm.diagramHint: A diagram is built as a graph, not typed as text. This creates a start→end skeleton to edit on the canvas.
strings.dr.generated: Generated from the graph — edit the flow on the canvas, not this text.
strings.dg.notDiagram: this memory is not a diagram
strings.dg.hint.connectSource: Connect: click the step the arrow leaves from.
strings.dg.hint.connectTarget: Connect: from '{key}' — now click the step it goes to.
strings.dg.hint.orphans: no path from the start to: {keys} — a connection is probably missing
strings.dg.selectPrompt: Click a step on the canvas to read its note, wire it up, or attach a memory to it.
strings.dg.label: label
strings.dg.labelHint: Keep the label objective — what the routine does here. Put the reasoning in the note.
strings.dg.notePh: why this step is the way it is, caveats, history…
strings.dg.linksHint: The flow says what happens; a linked memory says why.
strings.dg.jumpsHint: Where this step hands off to another flow — and the way back.
strings.dg.jump.openFrom: Open {title}, which continues into this step
strings.dg.jump.backTitle: Back to {title}, where this was reached from
strings.dg.jump.step.title: Where in {title}?
strings.dg.jump.step.label: step to land on
strings.dg.jump.step.hint: Naming a step selects it when that diagram opens. Leave it on the whole diagram when the handoff is not to one particular step.
strings.dg.jump.label: why it continues there
strings.dg.jump.labelPh: per store / on failure / manual review
strings.dg.newStep.title: New step
strings.dg.edgeLabel.title: Connect steps
strings.dg.edgeLabel.label: branch condition (optional)
strings.dg.confirmDelete.title: Delete step?
strings.dg.confirmDelete.body: '{key}' goes, and so do its connections and attached memories.
strings.dg.meta.name: title
strings.dg.meta.summaryPh: one line on what this routine is for…
strings.dg.mermaid.title: Mermaid source
strings.dg.mermaid.hint: Paste into anything that renders mermaid. It applies its own layout, so it will not match the canvas exactly.
strings.dgl.title: Diagrams
strings.dgl.intro: A flow is fixed by changing its shape, not its wording. The tools that check prose cannot see the problems listed below.
strings.dgl.filter: filter by title, summary, domain or tag…
strings.dgl.newBody: Creates a start and an end, then opens the editor to build the rest.
strings.dgl.jumpsWhy: steps that continue in another flow, or arrive from one
strings.dgl.documentedWhy: steps with a note explaining why
strings.dgl.emptyHint: A diagram maps one routine from start to finish, so a note can point at a single step. Create one here, or call the diagram() tool.
strings.dg.issueWhy.empty: The diagram has no steps at all.
strings.dg.issueWhy.no_start: No step is marked as the start, so there is no way into the flow.
strings.dg.issueWhy.many_starts: More than one step is marked as the start. A routine has one way in.
strings.dg.issueWhy.unreachable: Nothing connects to these steps from the start — usually a connection that was never drawn.
strings.dg.issueWhy.dead_end: The flow stops at these steps, but they are not marked as an end.
strings.dg.issueWhy.no_end: No step is marked as the end, so the flow never says where it stops.
strings.dg.readOnlyNote: Read-only. Turn on editing to change this step.
strings.dg.titleEdit: click to edit the title and summary
strings.dg.edge.editLabel: edit the condition on this line
strings.dg.editStep.title: Edit step
strings.dg.note.title: Note on '{key}'
strings.dg.note.hint: Hover the card to read this. The flow says what the routine does; the note says why it does it that way.
strings.dg.font.switch: text size on this diagram — stored, so everyone sees it
strings.toast.copyUnavailable: the clipboard is not available in this browser

strings.g.canvasAlt: Relations graph: {n} memories and {m} links, drawn as a force layout. The same records are listed in the Memories section.
strings.dg.canvasAlt: Flow diagram "{title}". The panel beside it lists each step with its connections and note, and the Mermaid button exports the whole flow as text.
